(b) 33-43 closes a round earlier than planned by moving BOTH ends toward each other instead of walking the leaf alone: 43 takes its last diagonal step to (15,23), and 33 slides three rows down its own column to (18,23). This is legal because col 18 is 33's locked axis (V to 45 above, V to 15 below, both survive a pure vertical slide) while its row was never locked - its only horizontal partner, 16, is an unaligned segment. That makes 33-43 horizontal on row 23. Winding at 33 is preserved: 15 stays N, 16 NE, 45 S, and 43 shifts from SW to W without passing any neighbour. Nothing else is reachable: 45-36, 58-16, 16-33, 38-13/23/18, 23-20 and 18-20 all have both endpoints locked on both axes by existing H/V chains, and the only free single-axis moves are blocked by collisions or would swallow a point (38 cannot take row 22 because 12 occupies it, nor row 11 because it would land on the 13-2 horizontal; 18 cannot take col 24 because the segment would then swallow 0). 39-42 is structurally impossible: row 42 is covered by horizontal segments continuously from col 2 to col 43, so the degree-1 leaf 42 can never be placed on it. The remaining diagonals 36-23, 36-58, 2-3 and 44-24 are all upgrade-blocked by an occupied target cell or a locked partner, so the alignment has converged.
